campaign.title: HTTP/2 Compliance Story: archived evidence assessment
limitations: Main paper completely reviewed; supporting literature review and independent full-fleet replication have explicit gaps.
Counts reproduce archived artifacts, not an independent live proxy campaign.
Missing/ambiguous worker evidence is retained; a timeout does not establish why a packet was not forwarded.
Designed protocol cases, versions and configurations are correlated; no inferential confidence intervals are justified.
Historical worker resources and exact UTC execution timestamps are missing; no substitutes are invented.

claims.description: 156 test cases, 78 client and 78 server, including 61 mirrored pairs
claims.evidence: Test definitions and pair mapping have exactly 156 IDs and 61 disjoint mirrored pairs.
claims.limitation: Census verifies the artifact, not every excluded MUST, SHOULD or TLS rule.

claims.evidence: 15 published proxy rows compared with exact counts under the authors classifier.
claims.limitation: Reanalysis of archived author measurements; counts are not independent fresh physical replication. Rejection is not equivalent to RFC compliance.

claims.description: Vectorized behavior differs by proxy and test identity
claims.evidence: All archived per-test author outcome vectors retained; aggregate counts checked against Table 5.
claims.limitation: Individual plotted raster cells not automatically verified against the PDF. Evidence-preserving recoding shown separately.

claims.evidence: Ten published client/server ratios independently transcribed from Figure 5; comparisons retain 78-case denominators.
claims.limitation: Paper broad E/G/R rule and ignore-to-drop rule reproduced; response scope/code and timeout causes need separate evidence.

claims.description: Behavior discrepancy over 61 explicitly paired test identities
claims.evidence: Published percentages compared within 0.05 percentage points for one-decimal rounding. Unknown pairs reported separately.
claims.limitation: Behavior discrepancy is descriptive, not evidence that code paths are redundant or a causal diagnosis.

claims.description: Historical versions change the distribution of protocol behaviors
claims.evidence: Explicit old-version pairs from Table 6 and all category changes preserved; prose changes tested in independent verifier.
claims.limitation: Version comparison is descriptive. No controlled experiment establishes that the new RFC caused the changes.

claims.description: H2H1 downgrade changes client-side behavior relative to H2EE
claims.evidence: Matched 78 client IDs; accepted means received in H2H1 and modified+unmodified in H2EE. Prose deltas preserved.
claims.limitation: No comparison of server-half tests to H2H1. Full deployment configuration is not reconstructed.

claims.description: No TLS versus plaintext behavioral differences
claims.evidence: Released TLS datasets are available for exact identity comparison.
claims.limitation: Unlabeled cleartext/TLS configurations cannot be assumed equivalent; observation from one deployment is not a universal layering guarantee.

claims.description: None of the studied proxies is fully compliant
claims.evidence: Broad author scores and evidence-preserving outcomes retained; acceptance and dropped categories require case-level semantics.
claims.limitation: Finite suite cannot establish full compliance. Error scope/code, modified messages and legitimate ignore rules require RFC interpretation.

claims.description: HTTP/2 proxies are stricter than prior HTTP/1.1 tests
claims.evidence: Published comparison is 1745/1950 rejected versus 128/564 HTTP/1.1. Appendix A maps eight prior case IDs into 23 current IDs.
claims.limitation: Different case universe, roles and versions prevent a matched causal improvement estimate; rejection includes silent drops.

claims.evidence: Section 2.1 says 12 bytes. Table 1 depicts 72 header bits; RFC9113 4.1 specifies nine octets. Independent raw-frame control planned.
claims.limitation: Expository unit/count error does not by itself invalidate the measurement campaign.

claims.description: Independent physical replication of all local and cloud proxy deployments
claims.evidence: Published local setup is Ubuntu 24.10 VMs on one hypervisor; cloud workers are Frankfurt and Melbourne Linode nodes on 2025-05-07.
claims.limitation: Those historical deployments, cloud internal versions and geographic paths cannot be recreated exactly. Fresh loopback pilot will be separate.

claims.description: TCP sequence matching confirms absence of transparent proxies
claims.evidence: Matching numbers exclude some TCP-splitting implementations.
claims.limitation: Does not exclude passive devices, non-splitting intermediaries, all path variants or TLS-layer intervention.

claims.description: Normative formal RFC compliance suites improve clarity/security
claims.evidence: Recommendation motivated by observed diversity and directly cited security literature.
claims.limitation: No randomized developer study, intervention, exploit reproduction or measured interoperability benefit.
